message.content:
Below is a concise overview of the key rights and protections you have as a residential tenant in Texas. These are drawn from Texas Property Code, local ordinances (where applicable), and federal law. If you need a more detailed explanation or help drafting a lease or complaint, let me know! | Area | What the law says | Practical Tips | |------|-------------------|----------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to **$1,000** for a single‑unit rental.
• Must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a written inventory of all items and their condition.
• Get a receipt for the deposit. | | **Habitability & Repairs** | • Landlord must keep the premises in a safe, livable condition (e.g., plumbing, heating, electrical).
• You can withhold rent only if the landlord fails to make necessary repairs after giving written notice. | • Document problems (photos, written notice).
• Send notice via certified mail or email with read receipt. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For month‑to‑month leases: **30‑day** written notice to terminate.
• For fixed‑term leases: you must honor the term unless the landlord breaches. | • Use a standard “Notice to Vacate” template. | | **Rent Increases** | • No statutory limit on how much a landlord can raise rent, but it must be in writing and given at least **30 days** before the increase takes effect. | • Review your lease for any “rent‑increase clause.” | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must serve a **10‑day** notice for nonpayment of rent or a **30‑day** notice for other violations.
• After the notice period, the landlord files an unlawful detainer action.
• You have the right to contest the eviction in court. | • Respond promptly to notices.
• Keep copies of all correspondence. | | **Discrimination** | • Protected classes: race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, source of income, etc.
• Landlords cannot refuse to rent or impose different terms because of these factors. | • File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights (TCHR) if you suspect discrimination. | | **Privacy / Entry** | • Landlord must give **reasonable notice** (usually 24 hours) before entering, except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of all entries. | | **Lease Terms** | • A lease is a binding contract; both parties must adhere to its terms.
• Unconscionable or illegal clauses (e.g., waiving your right to sue) are void. | • Read the lease carefully before signing. | | **Legal Assistance** | • Free or low‑cost legal aid is available through local bar associations, community legal clinics, and the Texas Legal Services Center. | • Contact your local legal aid office if you need representation. | ### Quick Checklist Before Signing a Lease 1. **Read the entire lease** – look for hidden fees, pet policies, subletting rules, and maintenance responsibilities. 2. **Ask for a copy of the property’s inspection report** (if available). 3. **Confirm the security deposit amount** and the conditions for its return. 4. **Verify that the landlord has a valid license** (if required by your city). 5. **Get everything in writing** – verbal agreements are hard to enforce. --- #### Need More Help? - **Drafting a lease**: I can generate a sample lease tailored to your situation. - **Complaint letter**: I can draft a formal notice to your landlord. - **Legal advice**: I can point you toward reputable legal aid resources in Texas. Just let me know what you’d like next!
